messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: private-edge-cluster-42 GPU queue growth > 95% for 3m. Autoscaler failed to add nodes (scale attempts hit capacity limits). Notifying #incidents and @oncall.

sam.k: I’m on it — paging @maya and @oncall-sre. Customer impacted: high latency and queued requests for dedicated private cluster behind VPC.

maya: looking now. +1 to high latency, seeing steady inflight queue growth on pool "edge-gpu-pool-42". Autoscaler logs show repeated `ScaleUpBlocked: quota_exceeded`.

oncall-sre: can you paste the most recent scaler error lines? I want to confirm if it’s quota or kube imagepulls delaying provisioning.

maya: snippet:
```
I0307 12:02:31 scaler.go:421] AttemptScaleUp: nodesRequested=4
E0307 12:02:33 cloudprovider.go:88] CreateInstance failed: quotaExceeded: cannot allocate GPUs in subnet-priv-az3
W0307 12:02:33 scaler.go:439] ScaleUpBlocked: reason=quota_exceeded, retry=backoff
```

sam.k: customer reported they recently reduced quota on that subnet for cost control. CS flagged it as expected but we still should failover to a different capacity tier.

eng-runtime-lead: we have compatible fallback pool (edge-gpu-fallback) in a different AZ, but routing policy currently sticky to customer's PV subnet. We can patch routing policy to allow cross-subnet fallback — doing a quick canary.

oncall-sre: blocking question — how long to route to fallback? If we patch routing, existing queued KV caches might not match and could cause token repetition. Need to coordinate with runbook.

maya: queue growth now 98% and 2000 waiting requests. Customers seeing 5-8s token latency -> now timeouts. We should alert affected customers via CS.

customer-success: I've messaged the primary customer contact with a short note: "We’re mitigating token queueing by routing to a fallback pool. Expect partial restoration within ~5–10m. We’ll follow up with a post-incident summary." They acknowledged.

sam.k: operational plan: (1) enable cross-subnet fallback routing for this customer (2) throttle low-priority background jobs (3) manually trigger scale on fallback pool to absorb queued work. Maya, can you run the routing patch? @eng-runtime-lead please stand by to monitor model compatibility.

maya: running patch now. command:
```
redwoodctl route update --customer cid-678 --allow-fallback=true --ttl 10m
```

maya: patch accepted by control-plane. Starting to drain and reassign requests; initiating scale on edge-gpu-fallback (requested +6 GPUs).

incident-bot: Control-plane event: route update applied for cid-678. 6 nodes provisioning in edge-gpu-fallback.

oncall-sre: seeing provisioning events but node bootstrap is slower than usual — `kubelet` waiting for image pull for runtime image `redwood/inference:opt-2026`.

maya: image pull rate is limited on that fallback AZ due to concurrent pulls across many customers. I'm switching to pre-warmed images on one node group.

eng-runtime-lead: alternative: spin up smaller-grain nodes with cached images (warm-warm group) — doubling init count for that group now.

sam.k: good. Also enable aggressive prefix cache reuse to reduce total new token work (reduces effective queue). Eng-runtime, push the KV-cache flag now.

eng-runtime-lead: toggled: `runtime.cache.prefix_reuse=high` for this customer on fallback pool.

oncall-sre: queue size dropping to 40% now. Latency back to 200–400ms for most requests. Some long-tail requests still time out.

ops-shift-lead: logging the incident as Sev-2 (customer-impacting latency for a paid customer). Noting cause: autoscaler blocked by subnet GPU quota + image-pull bottleneck on fallback pool.

customer-success: Customer sees partial recovery, will keep monitoring. They asked for ETA on full recovery.

sam.k: estimate full recovery in ~12–18 minutes once all warm nodes accept traffic. We should keep CS updated and prepare postmortem items: quota validation in onboarding, routing policy loosen for emergencies, and prewarming strategy for fallback pools.

incident-bot: Incident timeline recorded. Incident ID: INC-2026-2245678901. Current status: mitigated (partial), in progress (full recovery). Suggested next steps captured in runbook.

maya: handing off to @oncall-sre for monitoring during the remainder of the cooldown. I need to jump to a customer call. Will update if anything regresses.

oncall-sre: acknowledged — standing by. I’ll keep a 30m watch and escalate to eng-runtime if node bootstrap fails or queue rises >60%.

sam.k: thanks all. Post-incident, please add the customer quota flag to their account and add a proactive alert if subnet GPU quota < requested threshold. Closing the live page once stable for 30m.

incident-bot: Post-incident checklist reminder: add to postmortem, notify infra-scm to review image-pull limits, and schedule follow-up with CS within 24h.
